tab_intros.introduction: A web application for analysing mRNA translation dynamics using the SunTag fluorescence system.
tab_intros.introduction_tabs: Seven integrated modules cover the full analysis pipeline — from experiment design to kinetic parameter extraction.

tab_acquisition.intro: In this tab, you will estimate the optimal microscopy acquisition settings for a live-cell SunTag imaging experiment before data collection.
tab_acquisition.intro1: It is recommended that track length is at least 3 times the time to translate one (Suntag+protein).
tab_acquisition.intro2: The recommended frame rate should be lower that 1/3 of the time to translate the SunTag
tab_acquisition.math: The calculation is based on this equation : $$\Delta t = \frac{1}{2k}$$ where $$k$$ is the elongation rate.

tab_msd.intro: In this tab, you will calculate the MSD (Mean Square Displacement) of fluorescence dots in 3D.
tab_msd.math:
The calculation is based on this equation : 
 $$MSD = \langle\sum{(r_{t}-r_{t-1})^2}\rangle$$
where $$r_{t}$$ and $$r_{t-1}$$ are the position at time t and t-1.

tab_ribosome.intro: In this tab, you will estimate the number of ribosome on a translation site based on single protein fluorescence.
tab_ribosome.count_ribosome_col_note: After uploading your data, select a column in each dataframe that corresponds to the intensity.
tab_ribosome.math: The calculation is based on this equation : $$ d = \frac{I_{poly}}{I_{single_prot}(L_{poi}+0.5L_{tag})}$$ where $$I_{poi}$$ and $$I_{single_prot}$$ are the fluorescence of the polysome and single protein respectively ; $$L_{poi}$$ and $$L_{tag}$$ are the length of the protein of interest and the tag respectively.
tab_ribosome.select_csv_single: Choose your csv file that contains single protein fluorescence.
tab_ribosome.select_csv_polysome: Choose your csv file that contains polysome fluorescence.
tab_ribosome.after_upload: After uploading your data, select a column in each dataframe that corresponds to the intensity.

equations.g_exact:
$$
G(T)_{exact} = \frac{Pe^{-kT}}{P^2(\frac{N(N+1)}{2}+NM)^2 }[ \sum_{n=0}^{N}(N-n)(N-n+1)\frac{(2N+n+1)}{6}\frac{(kT)^n}{n!}
$$
$$
+ N\sum_{n=0}^{N}n\frac{(2N-n+1}{2}\frac{(kT)^n}{n!}+ N^2\frac{N+1}{2}\sum_{n=N}^{M}\frac{(kT)^n}{n!}
$$
$$+ N\sum_{n=1}^{N}n\frac{(1+n)}{2}\frac{(kT)^{M+N-n}}{(M+N-n)!}+ N^2\sum_{n=0}^{M}(M-n)\frac{(kT)^n}{n!} ]
$$
where $$c$$ is the initiation rate, $$k$$ the elongation rate and $$T$$ is the residence time. The steady state occupancy $$P$$ is defined by $$\frac{c}{k}$$.
equations.g_approx:
$$
G(T)_{approx} = \frac{T - x}{cT^2} H(T - x)
$$
where $$c$$ is the initiation rate, and $$T$$ is the residence time.

$$T=M/k$$ where $$M$$ is the RNA size (aa) and $$k$$ is the elongation rate.
equations.ribosome_density:
The calculation is based on this equation :
$$ d = \frac{I_{poly}}{I_{single\_prot}(L_{poi}+0.5L_{tag})}$$
where $$I_{poi}$$ and $$I_{single\_prot}$$ are the fluorescence of the polysome and single protein respectively; $$L_{poi}$$ and $$L_{tag}$$ are the length of the protein of interest and the tag respectively.

to_remove2.prot_length: Length of the protein in amino acid. This value will be added to suntag length.

to_remove2.fluo_one_suntag: Fluorescence of one suntag, used as reference for fluorescence profile.
to_remove2.retention_time: Protein stays at the RNA for some time.
to_remove2.pos_suntag: Choose if Suntag is before or after the protein.
to_remove2.noise: Add random noise to the protein fluorescence profile. 0 if no noise.
to_remove2.dt: Time step used to generate track. This value should be quite small regarding the time step used for the analysis.
to_remove2.track_length: Length duration of one track, used for the analysis.
to_remove2.nb_tracks: Number of tracks to be generated.
to_remove2.time_col: It corresponds to a FRAME column. This will be multiplied by the dt time step.

to_remove2.prot_length_analysis: Length of the protein in amino acid.
to_remove2.missing_point: How many continuous missing points can we recover. If it is too many the track will not be analysed. Missing points are created by calculating the mean value.
